title: Formal logic and critical reasoning
audience: a pre-law college student (any major) preparing for law school and the LSAT
purpose: Translate English into propositional and predicate logic, test validity with truth tables and proofs, master conditional reasoning, and analyze everyday arguments for assumptions and flaws.
primary_reading: forall x: Calgary, a free introduction to formal logic

blocks.deliverable: Identify the conclusion and premises of ten arguments.
Test five argument forms for validity with truth tables.
Translate 20 "if", "only if" and "unless" statements and write their contrapositives.
Week 7 midterm; prove three results and translate quantified sentences.
Name the flaw and the necessary assumption in ten short arguments.
Evaluate a causal claim from a study summary and an argument from analogy.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Argument audit: take a supplied 1,200-word op-ed written for the course, map its premises and conclusion, translate its key conditional claims, test their validity, and write a 1,000-word critique of its assumptions and flaws.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
